open_points.text: Inputs: "A ManifestOperation M10 with instance facts ..."; Enforces: "no selected instance (no name), no `api_base_url` (a name without one) ..."
open_points.question: How does `prepare_request` receive the selected instance *name* needed to distinguish `instance_not_selected` from `instance_address_missing`?
options: Add `selected_instance_name` (nullable) as an explicit input to `prepare_request`
Encode selected-instance presence/absence inside `ManifestOperation` itself and drop the separate-name distinction
Have `effects` pass an out-of-band flag/name from `check_binding_current` to `prepare_request`
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit nullable `selected_instance_name` input and keep both distinct error details.

open_points.text: Relations section: "A call that passes other arguments is a defect of its caller and answers `internal_error` ..."; public_op Errors: "`unknown_reference` for the whole call when any named identity does not exist"
open_points.question: Is `internal_error` for malformed relation arguments part of `store.read_records`' public error contract, or should such argument-shape failures be impossible/handled elsewhere?
options: Include `internal_error` in `store.read_records` Errors for malformed/ill-typed relation arguments
Forbid such calls at type/schema level and keep `store.read_records` Errors as `unknown_reference` only
Map malformed relation arguments to `refused` instead of `internal_error`
open_points.default_guess: Keep the Relations rule: malformed relation arguments return `internal_error` before any lookup.
